Looking at the cube [0,1]³, the plane through the three neighbors of each vertex gives eight planes, e.g. x+y+z=1, x+y+z=2, x−y−z=0, x−y−z=−1, −x+y−z=0, −x+y−z=−1, −x−y+z=0, −x−y+z=−1.

The piece containing the center (½,½,½) must satisfy all eight inequalities (it lies on the inner side of each cutting plane). The intersection of these half-spaces has vertices exactly at the six face centers of the cube: (½,½,0), (½,½,1), (½,0,½), (½,1,½), (0,½,½), (1,½,½). Each of the eight cutting planes contains three of these face centers (e.g. x+y+z=1 contains (½,½,0), (½,0,½), (0,½,½)), so the central piece has 8 equilateral triangular faces and 6 vertices — a regular octahedron.

Checking the options: (B) is a cube/parallelepiped, (C) is a cuboctahedron (which would arise only from shallower cuts), (D) is not the regular octahedron shape, and (E) is false since the center lies strictly inside one piece. The octahedron is figure (A).

\boxed{A}
